evals.name: WK-1
evals.expected_output: Six sections each in one table — last week, this week's matchup and lineup, waivers (the claim brief with a claim, pass or marginal verdict per detailed candidate — on this fixture the four rows the character budget keeps, each pass — the scramble list's players named from truncated_names with no claim verdict, as the tool gives them none, and the premium band), K and D/ST, injuries and byes, league activity — with a p10/p90 pair and its basis, the reads' as_of in the header, a Deadline column headed 'Deadline (ET)' (weekly's fixed header) in every table whose rows are actions — the lineup, the waiver brief, K and D/ST and the IR move under Injuries and byes — with a time on every move row (a lineup move's lock_at, a claim's next_run_at, an add now's lock time, an IR move's next run — the IR move a row of the Injuries and byes table) and '—' only on a row with no move, a held coin-flip swap on weekly's fixed line 'Top swap: coin flip — no move (<a> ↔ <b>, Δ <x>)' under the lineup table, never a table row (changelog §R16, R16-4), every move named outside a table with its time on its line, the Deadlines block as their summary, and the league settings read at most once. On this fixture the IR move is none: one IR seat is open and two bench players are eligible, so weekly prints injury-cascade's line under the Injuries and byes table, 'Also IR-eligible: "Tank Dell" (4366031, INJURY_RESERVE), "Rachaad White" (4697815, OUT) — the `espn-fantasy-football:roster-audit` Skill decides which, if any, to move to IR.', their rows '—' in Move and Deadline (changelog §R18, R18-5); each K and D/ST call the rec holds is the rec's own words — 'no claim clears the premium' for the K, 'no clear move: 2 on the scramble list after the run' for the D/ST — its row's Deadline '—'; and the byes of this week and the next two are on weekly's fixed line, one per week, naming who is out and making no plan — 'Byes, week 5: none of your starters.', 'Byes, week 6: none of your starters.', 'Byes, week 7: "James Cook III" (RB), "Bhayshul Tuten" (RB), "Cam Little" (K) — 2 at RB.' (changelog §R18, R18-8).

The skill called espn_project_players before espn_analyze_lineup and espn_record_recommendation last (tool_order)
The reply has all six section headings (regex: `Last week[\s\S]*matchup and lineup[\s\S]*Waivers[\s\S]*K and D/ST[\s\S]*Injuries and byes[\s\S]*League activity`)

The reply prints the reads' as_of — a date or a time after it, on weekly's fixed header 'Reads as of <as_of, ET>' or after weekly's term 'Data time', never 'as of' in prose (regex: `(?:\bas[_ ]of\b[^\n]{0,40}?|\bdata time\b[^\n]{0,60}?)(?:\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|\d{1,2}:\d{2}|\b\d{1,2}\s?[ap]\.?m\b|\b\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}\b|\b(?:jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec)[a-z]*\.?\s+\d{1,2}\b)`)

Every move the reply recommends outside a table's Deadline column — in a sentence, a list line, the Deadlines block or a table without that column — names when it is due: a time, or the waiver run or kickoff it is timed by. A pass, a hold or a row the tool holds is no move and needs none (weekly's held-swap line 'Top swap: coin flip — no move (<a> ↔ <b>, Δ <x>)' is one; on this fixture the moves due this week each name their time, and a note on a later week's byes that names who is out and makes no plan is no move due now and needs none — weekly's byes line 'Byes, week <N>: <starters out>.' is such a note, for week 7 'Byes, week 7: "James Cook III" (RB), "Bhayshul Tuten" (RB), "Cam Little" (K) — 2 at RB.' —, as are injury-cascade's line 'Also IR-eligible: <players> — the `espn-fantasy-football:roster-audit` Skill decides which, if any, to move to IR.', which hands the IR choice to roster-audit, and a K or D/ST call in the rec's own words, which the tool holds — 'no claim clears the premium' for the K, 'no clear move: 2 on the scramble list after the run' for the D/ST) (llm)

evals.name: WK-10
evals.$comment: R13-1: the eff setup judge stays one — 'once (the hand-off line)' and 'never again in the section or in Confidence & freshness' are one fact said two ways.
evals.prompt: What happened in my league this week?
evals.expected_output: On private-expiring the stored session still reads stored at Step 0 (espn_get_status: credential.state stored; espn_get_league: is_public false, from the settings the build's private-expiring-weekly seed left fresh, the only read it makes), so orient does not hand over. 'What happened in my league?' is weekly's League-activity-only scope (step 6 alone: no lineup, no projections), so under full the one read after Step 0 is espn_analyze_league_activity, and its first league read past the settings is the first read the cache does not serve: ESPN's 401 (changelog §R10, R10-28). E11 answers partial: true with its session-refusal lines: 'partial: the stored ESPN session was rejected, and ESPN's transaction feed needs one on a league not known to be public: the server's persisted history only; run `eff setup` in a terminal to replace it' and 'partial: the stored ESPN session was rejected, and ESPN's standings, rosters and free-agent pool need one on a league not known to be public: they were not read (by-team activity, waiver-order movement and rival needs go without them); run `eff setup` in a terminal to replace it' (exactly two lines ending 'to replace it'), with the history line 'no persisted transaction history yet, and ESPN's feed was not read: the window holds no transactions' and no teams line (both team reads were refused): the persisted history holds no transaction and the feed was not read, so the 7-day window shows 0 adds, drops, claims, losing claims and trades, with no waiver-order movement, standings movement or rival needs, and the rec is the digest 'league digest: 0 claims won, 0 lost, 0 trades in 7 days'. espn_get_status reads rejected from then on. weekly's P1 paragraph governs (changelog §R10, R10-11, R10-12): the League activity section is given from the persisted history and labelled partial — ESPN rejected the stored session, so the feed, the standings, the rosters and the free-agent pool were not read, and by-team activity, waiver-order movement and rival needs go without them — with the one command, eff setup in a terminal, given once, in the hand-off line that ends the answer; Confidence & freshness says the section is partial for that reason (its first line orient's 'Partial: ESPN rejected the stored session — not read: …'); espn_analyze_league_activity is called once, never repeated for these lines (a repeat reads nothing more); and on this private league the answer ends with the hand-off to the session-check Skill (changelog §R10, R10-7). No other section of the briefing and no lineup call — weekly's League-activity-only answer: the League activity section, Confidence & freshness and Attribution, with no Deadlines block and no Not actionable here list (changelog §R12, R12-2): a reply that runs another step first takes the 401 there and ends at the hand-off before E11. No Session line about keyless reads: the league is private. A run that calls espn_check_auth before the first read the cache does not serve is graded like any other: the accepting probe moves the label to validated and leaves the 401 armed, so that read still takes ESPN's 401 and the label moves to rejected (changelog §R10, R10-33); no run is voided for probing.
expectations: espn_analyze_league_activity was called exactly once — never repeated for its session-refusal lines (tool_used: min 1 max 1)
espn_analyze_lineup was not called — the question is the League activity section only, weekly's scope rule (tool_used: min 0 max 0)

The answer hands over to the session-check Skill (regex: `\bsession-check\b`)

The League activity section reports the server's persisted history — 0 adds, drops, claims and trades in the 7-day window, empty on this seed (weekly's fixed line 'Partial — the server's persisted history only: <a> adds, <d> drops, <c> claims, <t> trades in the 7-day window; not read: <the refused reads> (by-team activity, waiver-order movement and rival needs go without them).' reports it, with 0 for each) (llm)

No other section of the briefing is given: weekly's League-activity-only answer is the League activity section, Confidence & freshness and Attribution (orient's opening lines — on this fixture its seeding line 'seeding reading unconfirmed — assuming ESPN's rule; run `espn-fantasy-football:onboard` to record it' — and the closing hand-off line 'Hand-off: the `espn-fantasy-football:session-check` Skill takes it from here — `eff setup` in a terminal.' are not sections) — no lineup, matchup, waivers, K and D/ST or injuries section, no Deadlines block and no Not actionable here list (on this fixture the League activity section may give the window's counts in a table, the reads it did not make marked 'not read', with a sentence on what its zeros mean, bold or not: all of that is the section's own, as everything under Confidence & freshness, whatever its bullets, is that section's — no other section) (llm)

The answer ends with the hand-off line to session-check (orient's fixed hand-off line 'Hand-off: the `espn-fantasy-football:session-check` Skill takes it from here — `eff setup` in a terminal.') (llm)

No Session line about keyless reads: the league is private.
